sections.heading: Situation Overview
sections.body:
Project Meridian represents a potential $210 million acquisition of Kestrelbrook Health Partners (Meridian Health Partners), an outpatient healthcare services provider founded in 2013 and headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina.

The business operates a network of outpatient diagnostic imaging and specialty care clinics across the Carolinas. Key operating characteristics include:
- Service delivery under long-term agreements with regional health systems and independent physician groups.
- Senior leadership team with an average tenure of 13 years in outpatient healthcare operations.
- Stated growth strategy focused on same-site volume expansion, de novo clinic rollouts in adjacent Carolinas markets, and tuck-in acquisitions of independent specialty practices.

evidence.quote: The senior leadership team averages 13 years in outpatient healthcare operations.
Growth strategy centers on same-site volume growth, de novo clinic openings in adjacent Carolinas metros, and selective tuck-in acquisitions of independent specialty practices.

sections.heading: Financial Performance & Benchmarking
sections.body:
Historical financial performance demonstrates steady revenue expansion and EBITDA margin progression from FY22 to FY24:
- FY22: Revenue of $34.2 million, gross margin of 57.8%, and EBITDA of $5.9 million (17.3% margin).
- FY23: Revenue of $39.6 million (15.8% growth), gross margin of 58.9%, and EBITDA of $7.6 million (19.2% margin).
- FY24: Revenue of $45.8 million (15.7% growth), gross margin of 60.1%, and EBITDA of $9.8 million (21.4% margin).

Relative to industry peers (Meadowlark Imaging Partners, Wrenfield Specialty Clinics, and Brightpath Diagnostic Group):
- FY24 revenue growth of 15.7% exceeds the peer median of 11.0% by 4.7 percentage points.
- FY24 gross margin of 60.1% tracks below the peer median of 63.4% by 3.3 percentage points.
- Peer EV/EBITDA trading multiples show a median of 21.0x.

sections.heading: Portfolio Fit & Concentration Impact
sections.body:
The proposed transaction requires an equity investment based on a $210 million deal size, expanding total portfolio assets under management from $770 million to $980 million.

Key portfolio implications include:
- Healthcare Services exposure increases from $231 million (30.0% of existing portfolio across Palmetto Diagnostic Group) to $441 million (45.0% post-transaction).
- Exposure to Industrials declines from 34.9% to 27.4%.
- Exposure to Fintech declines from 19.5% to 15.3%.
- Exposure to Consumer declines from 15.6% to 12.2%.

The 15.0 percentage-point concentration increase requires explicit Investment Committee evaluation against target portfolio allocation limits.

sections.heading: Key Risks & Diligence Findings Requiring Confirmation
sections.body:
Two material discrepancies have been identified during crosscheck analysis:

Contractual Revenue Durability:
- Management reports that 80% of FY24 revenue is recurring under multi-year contracts.
- Review of customer contracts reveals that agreements with Cinderwood Health System ($5.2 million), Thistlebrook Specialty Partners ($4.6 million), and Fenwick Diagnostic Alliance ($4.4 million) contain 30-day termination for convenience clauses.
- These cancellable agreements represent $14.2 million, or 31.0% of FY24 revenue, leaving only $22.1 million (48.3% of FY24 revenue) protected under multi-year commitments terminable solely for cause.

Cap Table and Option Dilution:
- The May 15, 2026 capitalization table reports 7,850,000 fully diluted shares, reflecting 520,000 issued early employee options.
- Option grant records show four additional board-approved grants dated between March 18, 2026, and May 9, 2026, totaling 232,000 options (VP Payer Contracting: 68,000; Director of Ambulatory Growth: 58,000; Head of Data & Clinical Analytics: 52,000; VP HR: 54,000).
- Including these grants increases the fully diluted share count to 8,082,000 shares, resulting in unmodeled dilution of 2.9%.

sections.heading: Next Steps & Workstreams
sections.body:
To advance diligence and resolve identified discrepancies, the deal team recommends the following actions:
- Reconcile the fully diluted share count with company legal counsel to reflect the 232,000 board-approved option grants issued between March and May 2026.
- Review historical customer retention and renewal rates for Cinderwood Health System, Thistlebrook Specialty Partners, and Fenwick Diagnostic Alliance to determine historical churn behavior under 30-day termination provisions.
- Present portfolio concentration analysis to the Investment Committee to determine whether a 45.0% Healthcare Services weighting requires risk mitigation or syndicate participation.
- Complete financial and tax diligence to verify margin bridge from FY22 (17.3% EBITDA margin) to FY24 (21.4% EBITDA margin).
